claim: The cursor carves a wake across the surface — a V of cresting ripples trailing its path, fading like water behind a boat. Card preserved.

q1_defects.answer: Multiple blocking defects. (1) NO MOTION: all four play frames are byte-identical (md5 4b0ce859ac92979b1ef92c34a0a75026; metrics frameDeltaMag=0 for play-1/2/3). The pointer-wake animation never animates across the captured sequence. (2) THREE DEAD CONTROLS: trailLength, waveSpeed and decayRate are byte-identical across low/mid/high (md5 4b5ce3d53827b48f2c09d0317746d8cc; metrics changed=false, meanAbsDiff=0). Only amplitude is live. NOT a placeholder-slab defect — the real card content (brass header, blue dot, grey rows) is preserved in every frame, and content is tack-sharp.

q2_reads_as.answer: Does NOT read as the claim at premium quality. The claim is a moving V of cresting ripples trailing the cursor, fading like a boat wake. The play sequence shows zero motion, so the defining trailing-wake behavior is absent. The only visible distortion (in the amplitude sweep) is a single static curved refraction arc that bends the text rows — a generic lens/bulge bend, not a V, not a trail, not a fade. The real card look IS preserved and distorted (passes the texture-preservation invariant), but the effect is not legible as a wake.
evidence: pointer-wake-wave/after/control-amplitude-high.png shows a single static curved refraction arc bending the rows, not a V of trailing ripples
pointer-wake-wave/after/play-2.png shows no wake motion vs idle.png
metrics: play frames frameDeltaMag=0 — no trailing-ripple animation

q3_discoverable.answer: Weakly discoverable and misleading. idle.png shows a clean, legible card with only a faint static sheen — it does not telegraph a wake. When driven, the effect produces no motion (play frames identical), so a user toggling it would assume it is broken. The amplitude knob is the only way to see anything happen.
evidence: pointer-wake-wave/after/idle.png clean card, faint static central sheen only
pointer-wake-wave/after/control-amplitude-low.png vs control-amplitude-high.png is the only visible state change

q4_responsive.answer: Mostly UNresponsive. Only 1 of 4 controls (amplitude) visibly changes the look: amplitude-low is near-flat with a soft central highlight while amplitude-high shows a pronounced curved displacement arc bending the rows (metrics pixelDiff meanAbsDiff=1.112). The other three controls — trailLength, waveSpeed, decayRate — are completely dead (byte-identical low/mid/high, meanAbsDiff=0). trailLength and waveSpeed are exactly the knobs that would shape a wake, and both are inert.
evidence: pointer-wake-wave/after/control-amplitude-low.png (near-flat) vs control-amplitude-high.png (strong curved displacement bending rows)

q5_net.answer: ANNOYED. The card content is preserved and one control is live, but the primitive fails on its defining behavior: it produces no motion at all (the play sequence is frozen), it does not read as a trailing wake, and three of its four controls — including the two most wake-relevant ones — are dead. A user would conclude the effect is broken.
evidence: pointer-wake-wave/after/control-amplitude-high.png shows a static bulge, not a V wake

mustFix.issue: No animation / no wake: all four play frames (idle, play-1, play-2, play-3) are byte-identical and frameDeltaMag=0, so the cursor-driven trailing wake never moves. The primitive's defining behavior does not render over time.
